title: Empagliflozin in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Undergoing On-Pump CABG: The POST-CABGDM Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Pitta FG; Lima EG; Tavares CAM; Martins EB; Rached FH; Moreira EM; Mioto BM; Lottenberg SA; Bolta PMP; Justino LG; Favarato D; Carvalho LNS; Pinesi HT; Barbosa CTM; Dallan LAO; Dallan LRP; Barbosa MHM; Kalil Filho R; de Lemos JA; Serrano CV
study_design: Single-center, investigator-initiated, pragmatic, randomized, open-label trial with blinded outcome adjudication (modified intention-to-treat analysis)
setting: Instituto do Coração, Hospital das Clínicas, University of São Paulo; tertiary academic hospital; single-center elective on-pump CABG program
analysis_population: Modified intention-to-treat: all randomized patients who underwent surgery (n=145; 71 empagliflozin, 74 control)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), planned on-pump; 9 procedures were performed off-pump due to intraoperative decisions
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 25 mg orally once daily plus standard care for at least 3 months prior to CABG; discontinued 72 hours before surgery
exposure_timing: Preoperative initiation ≥3 months before surgery; drug stopped 72 h pre-op
follow_up: Primary AKI assessed within 7 days post-surgery; secondary and safety outcomes assessed during hospitalization and up to 30 days after surgery
funding: No external funding; supported by resources from the Atherosclerosis Unit, Instituto do Coração, Hospital das Clínicas HCFMUSP, University of São Paulo
conflicts_of_interest: Some authors reported personal fees/DSMB roles with industry (e.g., Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly, J&J, Merck, AstraZeneca); no other conflicts reported for the remaining authors
extraction_notes: Trial registered NCT04523064. AKI adjudicated blinded to treatment; secondary outcomes not adjudicated.
overall_extraction_notes: Secondary outcomes included AF and type 5 MI (not prespecified in this project). Length of stay was not directly reported as mean/SD; only hospital-free days were provided, so no LOS data extracted.

title: The effects of sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibition on cardiac surgery-associated acute kidney injury: An open-label randomized pilot study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Rampanelli E; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
study_design: Prospective, single-center, open-label, phase IV, randomized, parallel-group controlled pilot trial (1:1). Intention-to-treat analysis.
setting: Tertiary academic hospital (Amsterdam UMC); adult elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass.
intervention_or_exposure: Empagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily from three days before surgery until postoperative day two.
exposure_timing: Started 3 days preoperatively; continued through postoperative day 2.
follow_up: Biomarkers on POD1 and POD2; AKI incidence within 7 days post-surgery; intraoperative ketones; in-hospital complications.
funding: European Union Horizon 2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No. 101024833.
conflicts_of_interest: One author (DHR) reported consulting and research funding from multiple pharmaceutical companies; all honoraria paid to employer. Other authors declared no conflicts.
extraction_notes: Trial was stopped early at ~75% enrollment due to observed AKI difference. Supplementary tables with detailed complications not available in provided text.
overall_extraction_notes: Mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events, postoperative heart failure, and total hospital length of stay were not extractable from the provided text (reported only as part of supplementary material or not reported).

title: Dapagliflozin and Acute Kidney Injury Following Cardiac Surgery: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Hulst AH; de Oliveira NPM; Niesten ED; Wietsma NE; Gerritse BM; Scohy TV; Rettig TCD; Snellen FTF; Voogd MF; Godfried MB; de Boer RN; Wink J; van der Werff LMM; Cobbaert CM; Ruhaak LR; Eberl S; Preckel B; Hollmann MW; Schenk J; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; MERCURI-2 Study Group
study_design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled superiority trial (RCT).
setting: Seven hospitals (2 academic, 5 nonacademic). Adult elective cardiac surgery patients.
analysis_population: Intention-to-treat for primary outcome (392 vs 392). Per-protocol exploratory analysis included patients who took all 4 doses.
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiac surgery including CABG, valve repair/replacement, and aortic root/arch procedures; majority with cardiopulmonary bypass.
intervention_or_exposure: Dapagliflozin 10 mg orally once daily, 4 total doses: evening before surgery, morning of surgery, postoperative day 1, and postoperative day 2.
exposure_timing: Initiated 1 day prior to surgery and continued through postoperative day 2 (4 doses).
comparator: Matching placebo administered on the same schedule.
follow_up: Primary outcome assessed within 7 postoperative days; secondary outcomes (e.g., MACE) at 30 days; postoperative adverse events during the postoperative period.
funding: Supported by The Netherlands Organization for Health Research and Development (ZonMw, grant 10140022010003). Additional investigator funding from EU Horizon 2020 (Marie Skłodowska-Curie 101024833), ESAIC/BJA Charity, ZonMw (Veni-09150162410006), Dutch Diabetes Foundation, and Dutch Kidney Foundation.
conflicts_of_interest: Reported: grants/fees outside the submitted work for multiple authors. Examples: funding from Roche Diagnostics (Rettig), ESAIC/ZonMw (Preckel), editorial roles (Hollmann), grants/advisory boards with AstraZeneca, Boehringer Ingelheim, Eli Lilly, MSD, Novo Nordisk, Sidero Bio (van Raalte). Others reported no disclosures.
overall_extraction_notes: No explicit data for in-hospital mortality or euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis were reported. Ketoacidosis was listed as a safety event (1 vs 0) without specifying euglycemic status, so it was not extracted under the EDKA outcome.

title: Perioperative dapagliflozin in diabetic patients undergoing cardiac surgery: the DAPA-CS trial.
authors: Li Z; Chen R; Han J; Zhou H; Zeng Z; Zhao Y; Liu S; Zhang H; Zheng Z
setting: Single-centre tertiary cardiac surgery hospital (Fuwai Hospital, Beijing)
analysis_population: Modified intention-to-treat: randomized patients who underwent surgery; 164 analyzed (81 dapagliflozin, 83 control)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective on-pump cardiac surgery (predominantly isolated on-pump CABG)
exposure_timing: Administered for at least 3 days preoperatively; withheld on day of surgery; resumed postoperatively once oral intake was re-established through POD 5
follow_up: Perioperative biomarker endpoints through 120 h post-op; clinical events assessed at 30 days and 12 months
funding: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences Innovation Fund for Medical Sciences (2021-I2M-1-063); Noncommunicable Chronic Diseases–National Science and Technology Major Project (2024ZD0521904); National High-Level Hospital Clinical Research Funding (2023-GSP-GG-20, 2022-GSP-GG-28); National Clinical Research Center for Cardiovascular Diseases (NCRC2020004)
conflicts_of_interest: Authors report no disclosures of interest
extraction_notes: Primary endpoint was myocardial injury (hs-cTnI), not part of the prespecified outcomes for this review. AKI was a key secondary endpoint. Safety outcomes included DKA. MACE at 30 days and 12 months were reported narratively without extractable counts in the provided material.
overall_extraction_notes: Data for several prespecified outcomes (in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE counts, and length of hospital stay) were not explicitly reported or extractable from the provided figures/text. Only AKI (reported-effect) and DKA (zero events) could be reliably extracted.

title: Preoperative Exposure to Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitors and Acute Kidney Injury After Cardiac Surgery: A Retrospective Single-Centre Cohort Study With Overlap Weighting Propensity Score Analysis.
authors: Ruste M; Vieira A; Le Guennec-Lux Y; Berthod C; Pozzi M; Mewton N; Fellahi JL; Jacquet-Lagrèze M
study_design: Single-centre retrospective cohort with overlap-weighted propensity score causal analysis
setting: Cardiovascular and thoracic centre of a teaching hospital (Hôpital Louis Pradel, Hospices Civils de Lyon)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass and with ≥1 indication for long-term SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (T2D with high CV risk, LVEF <50%, or CKD with eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Exclusions included eGFR <20, type 1 diabetes, preop AKI, transplant/LT-MCS, preop cardiogenic shock, death before POD1, and CKD conditions without SGLT2i indication.
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative long-term SGLT2 inhibitor medication recorded on preoperative prescriptions; discontinuation defined as withdrawal ≥3 days before surgery per ESC guidance
exposure_timing: Preoperative exposure (with variable continuation or discontinuation before surgery)
follow_up: AKI assessed within 7 days post-surgery by KDIGO creatinine criteria; other outcomes during index hospitalization/ICU stay
funding: No specific grant from public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors
conflicts_of_interest: Authors report no conflicts of interest.
extraction_notes: Propensity score model variables: LVEF category, chronic arterial hypertension, COPD, BMI, preop hemoglobin, preop serum creatinine, loop diuretic, renin–angiotensin system inhibitors, surgery type, and simplified prediction index for RRT. Overlap weighting used for causal relative risks.
overall_extraction_notes: Primary outcomes on AKI were primarily reported as overlap-weighted causal relative risks; raw counts before weighting are also tabulated. ICU length of stay was reported, but total hospital length of stay was not reported; postoperative heart failure and MACE were not reported.

title: Impact of Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter 2 Inhibitors on Acute Kidney Injury Post Off-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Retrospective Cohort Study and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Zhou X; Pan Y; Hua K; Yang X
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort with 1:3 propensity score matching
setting: Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Department of Cardiovascular Surgery (tertiary academic center)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (OPCABG) meeting inclusion/exclusion criteria; comparison of preoperative dapagliflozin users vs non-users after PSM
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative dapagliflozin 10 mg once daily (SGLT2 inhibitor)
exposure_timing: Minimum 3 months of uninterrupted therapy preoperatively; stopped 72 hours before surgery
follow_up: AKI assessed within 48 hours after OPCABG; other outcomes assessed during index hospitalization
funding: This research received no external funding.
conflicts_of_interest: The authors declare no conflict of interest.
extraction_notes: AKI definition per study: increase in serum creatinine ≥0.3 mg/dL (26.2 µmol/L) or 1.5–2-fold from baseline within 48 hours after OPCABG (Methods).
overall_extraction_notes: Study limited to off-pump CABG population; only dapagliflozin users included in exposure group. No numerical data reported for length of hospital stay, postoperative heart failure, MACE, or euglycemic DKA in the provided text/tables.

title: Preoperative SGLT2i therapy and acute kidney injury in patients undergoing emergency and urgent coronary artery bypass grafting - A causal inference framework.
authors: Kolland M; Sartori S; Klivinyi C; Schörghuber M; Pannold J; Knez I; Kirsch AH; Schreiber N
study_design: Single-center retrospective cohort with causal inference weighting (entropy balancing)
setting: Medical University of Graz, Department of Cardiac Surgery (tertiary academic hospital)
analysis_population: Adults undergoing urgent (<48 h) or emergent (≤12 h) isolated CABG with an indication for SGLT2i (T2DM, HFrEF, or CKD). Exclusions: age <18, missing key labs for AKI definition, postoperative mechanical circulatory support, preoperative KRT, reoperation within 72 h, preoperative sepsis/septic shock.
surgery_or_procedure: Urgent or emergent isolated coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG)
intervention_or_exposure: Preoperative SGLT2 inhibitor therapy (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin)
exposure_timing: Documented SGLT2i use within 2 weeks prior to surgery
comparator: No preoperative SGLT2i use (within 2 weeks prior to surgery)
follow_up: AKI assessed up to 7 days post-op; ICU length of stay during index hospitalization; 30-day all-cause mortality; postoperative diabetic ketoacidosis assessed days 1–7.
conflicts_of_interest: Authors declared no known competing interests.
overall_extraction_notes: Study limited to urgent/emergent isolated CABG. AKI defined solely by creatinine-based KDIGO criteria; urine output not used. Mortality reported at 30 days (not strictly in-hospital); definition preserved in outcome_definition.

title: Cardiovascular Outcomes of Perioperative Sodium-Glucose Transporter 2 Inhibition in Cardiac Surgery Patients: An Open-Label Randomized Pilot Study.
authors: Snel LIP; Oosterom-Eijmael MJP; Lankadeva YR; Plummer MP; Preckel B; Zuurbier CJ; Hermanides J; van Raalte DH; Hulst AH
setting: Amsterdam University Medical Center; elective cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted adult cardiac surgery; ICU postoperative monitoring
analysis_population: Intention-to-treat (all 55 randomized participants from MERCURI trial included)
surgery_or_procedure: Elective cardiopulmonary bypass-assisted cardiac surgery (mostly valve repair/replacement or combined with CABG)
exposure_timing: Administered from 3 days preoperatively until 2 days postoperatively
follow_up: Hemodynamic and fluid outcomes assessed during the first 24 postoperative hours; other postoperative observations reported without quantified time horizon
funding: European Union Horizon 2020 Marie Skłodowska-Curie grant agreement No. 101024833
conflicts_of_interest: One author (D.H.v.R.) reports consultancy/honoraria and research funding from Boehringer Ingelheim, Lilly, Merck, Sanofi, AstraZeneca; honoraria paid to employer. Others report no conflicts.
extraction_notes: This sub-study focuses on hemodynamics, fluids, vasoactive support, AF, and CK-MB. Prespecified review outcomes (AKI, mortality, heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA, length of stay) were not quantitatively reported here; AKI findings were primarily reported in the parent MERCURI publication cited as ref. 11.
overall_extraction_notes: No analysis-ready data were reported for the prespecified outcomes (postoperative AKI, in-hospital mortality, postoperative heart failure, MACE, euglycemic DKA, or length of hospital stay). The paper states in the Conclusion that SGLT2 inhibition was not associated with increased risk of AKI, hypotension, or arrhythmias, but provides no quantitative data or definitions suitable for meta-analysis. Therefore, outcome fields are left empty per protocol.
